name: Cartouche
subtitle: Cartouche itself
description: The source Cartouche's built-in SideStore reads for Cartouche's own updates. It lists Cartouche and nothing else: Cartouche never lists, hosts or downloads games.

apps.name: Cartouche
apps.subtitle: Play your own games built with nxnative
apps.localizedDescription: Cartouche runs the games you build with nxnative from your own copies, renews itself without a computer, and gives them Increased Memory Limit. It never downloads a game.

versions.localizedDescription:
Install it with iloader, from scratch or over 0.1.1: nothing to set in SideStore or anywhere else.

- iloader: in Manage Pairing File, Place In All Apps now puts the pairing file into Cartouche, listed there as LiveContainer. No export, no AirDrop. Cartouche keeps its name on the home screen.
- Setup: the pairing file step ticks itself, even while you are still at the computer. Sign in with SideStore opens LocalDevVPN, then the Apple ID sign-in, and brings you back to Cartouche once you are signed in.
- The built-in SideStore signs in through the SideStore (New) anisette server, as iloader does, no longer asks for a pairing file it already has, and accepts the one iloader exports.
- A pairing file exported from iloader can also be opened with Cartouche, from AirDrop or Files.

Install this version once with iloader, over Cartouche 0.1.0: your games and data stay.

- iloader now gives Cartouche its certificate, as it does for LiveContainer+SideStore. Cartouche hands it to LiveContainer by itself, which signs your games with it: no file to import, no button.
- Setup, at the top of Games until it is done: your pairing file from iloader, then signing in once in the built-in SideStore. Play leads there while the certificate is missing.
- Lab: Python now writes its files in UTF-8, so nxnative's rewriter no longer stops on sdk.
- Cartouche now takes the place of a LiveContainer+SideStore on the iPhone, since iloader gives both the same app group.

First test build of Cartouche.

- Games: the catalogue of supported games, your own first, with a sheet for each that says how it should run on this iPhone.
- System: the memory limit iOS gives Cartouche, the days left before its signature expires, Renew now, renewing every night from Shortcuts, and expiry alerts.
- System › Lab: rewrites the code of your own game on this iPhone with nxnative's rewriter, then compares each file with your Mac's build. A test for building games on the iPhone later.
- The built-in SideStore asks for Increased Memory Limit on free accounts, and never revokes a certificate.
